verdicts.title: SFT loss-only DFT evaluation scores an unscaled-logit objective: `_fused_dft_loss_only` routes prediction_loss_only=True through `fused_dft_loss`, which ignores config logit scaling, so eval_loss measures a different objective than training on Cohere/Cohere2/Granite
verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced end to end on this tree, and every link of the chain verified in the current source. (1) _sft_trainer.py:216-220 `_fused_loss_eligible = loss_type in ('nll','dft') and not self._log_completion_metrics and compute_loss_func is None`, and `_sft_config.py:90 log_completion_metrics: bool = True`, so at defaults `_fused_dft` is False. (2) :233-235 `_fused_dft_loss_only = args.loss_type == 'dft' and self._lm_head_param_name is not None` deliberately drops the eligibility gate. (3) :596 `elif self._fused_dft or (not return_logits and self._fused_dft_loss_only):` -> :604 `loss = fused_dft_loss(hidden, lm_head_weight, inputs['labels'])`. (4) :666-670 `self._get_eval_per_example_loss_fn(return_logits=not prediction_loss_only)`, and _dp_trainer.py:3187 `prediction_loss_only=True if self._compute_metrics is None else None`. (5) `fused_dft_loss` (_dft.py:141-147) has no scale argument at all: the CUDA/chunked branch calls `linear_nll_sum(...)` which pins logit_scale to 1.0 (_fused_lce.py:113-114 `Opaque_LinearCrossEntropyLoss.apply(hidden, weight, labels, -100, 0, 0.0, use_token_scaling, 1.0)`; the non-CUDA branch at :119-122 passes no scale either), and the eager fallback is `dft_loss(hidden_states @ lm_head_weight.transpose(-2,-1), labels)`. Meanwhile the non-fused `else` branch (:606-615) scores `self._loss_fn(out.logits, labels)` on HF's scaled logits (transformers 5.15.1 CohereForCausalLM: `logits = logits * self.logit_scale`; GraniteForCausalLM: `logits = logits / self.config.logits_scaling`). Verified the model classes are supported families (AGENTS.md lists Cohere/Cohere2/Granite). Primitive-level measurement (per-example, 2x12 tokens, tiny configs): llama train==loss-only to 0.000%, cohere (logit_scale=0.0625 default) 0.610%, granite(logits_scaling=8.0) 2.085%, granite(logits_scaling=1.0) 0.000%; the loss-only value equals `dft_loss(hidden @ W.T, labels)` exactly in every case, i.e. it is the unscaled-logit objective. Trainer-level measurement, built exactly like the repo's own `_dft_trainer` fixture but with a tiny CohereForCausalLM: eval_loss(compute_metrics=None) = 0.060834 vs eval_loss(compute_metrics=lambda ep: {}) = 0.064736 = the training-objective reference dft_loss(model(...).logits) 0.064736 -> 6.03% divergence; the same fixture with the repo's LlamaForCausalLM gives 0.063958 in all three modes. That is exactly the inconsistency `test_sft_dft_eval_loss_consistent_across_metric_modes` (test_trl_trainers.py:2030-2037) exists to catch, and it passes only because `_dft_trainer` uses `_tiny_model()` = LlamaForCausalLM (line 41-51), which has no logit scaling. Sibling confirmed by direct construction: with `log_completion_metrics=False` on a Cohere model, `_fused_dft` is True (printed True/True/eligible=True vs False/True/False at the default), so `fused_dft_loss` becomes the *training* objective and DP-SFT silently optimizes an unscaled-temperature DFT loss. Refutation attempts that failed: no logit-scale plumbing exists anywhere in opaque-alignment (grep for logit_scale/logits_scaling under packages/opaque-alignment returns nothing); no gate excludes scaled families from `_fused_dft_loss_only`; the CPU path is not a rescue because the chunked branch is equally unscaled. Not tracked: no open issue covers it (906/905 are wandb metric-naming bugs; 862 is fp32 logit upcasting for numerics). Severity kept high rather than raised: it needs the opt-in `loss_type='dft'` (SFTConfig default is 'nll', _sft_config.py:80) plus one of three logit-scaled families, so it is not a defaults-only silent failure, but within that combination eval_loss/best-model selection and (with log_completion_metrics=False) the trained objective are silently wrong, and no privacy guarantee is involved.
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: `SFTTrainer(model=<CohereForCausalLM|Cohere2ForCausalLM|GraniteForCausalLM with logits_scaling != 1>, args=SFTConfig(loss_type='dft', ...))`. Whenever evaluation runs without `compute_metrics` (DPTrainer.evaluate passes prediction_loss_only=True, _dp_trainer.py:3187), `prediction_step` takes the logits-free closure and scores `fused_dft_loss`, which computes DFT against the raw `hidden @ lm_head.T` projection with logit_scale pinned to 1.0. Measured on this tree with the repo's own DFT trainer fixture and a tiny Cohere: eval_loss = 0.060834 while the training objective (and the eval_loss reported when compute_metrics IS configured) = 0.064736 - a 6.0% divergence, so the same checkpoint reports two different eval losses depending only on whether compute_metrics is set, and `metric_for_best_model='eval_loss'` / early stopping select on the wrong objective. Llama is unaffected (0.000%), which is why the existing consistency test passes. Granite diverges only when the checkpoint sets logits_scaling != 1 (2.1% measured at logits_scaling=8.0 on the primitive); Cohere always diverges (logit_scale default 0.0625). Sibling, same root cause: with `log_completion_metrics=False`, `_fused_dft` becomes True (verified) and the unscaled DFT loss becomes the *training* objective for these families, silently. No privacy impact.

verdicts.title: The fused-CE wrapper's non-fused fallback branch recomputes logits without family logit scaling, silently changing the trained objective on the CUDA fp32 path
verdicts.reasoning: The arithmetic defect is reproduced directly and the reachability chain is verified except for executing on a GPU (this sandbox is CPU-only, torch.cuda.is_available() == False). Code as it stands: cross_entropy.py:281-291 `use_fused_ce = loss_only and _fused_linear_ce_loss_is_supported(logits_to_keep, kwargs) and ((hidden_states.is_cuda and hidden_states.dtype in (torch.bfloat16, torch.float16)) or not hidden_states.is_cuda)`; the `if use_fused_ce:` branch resolves `logit_scale = config.logit_scale / config.logits_scaling` and `softcap = config.final_logit_softcapping` (:310-323) and forwards them into the kernel (:336); the `else` branch (:354-364) does only `logits = self.lm_head(hidden_states[:, slice_indices, :])` then `loss = self.loss_function(logits, labels, self.vocab_size, **kwargs)` - it reproduces stock Llama's tail and applies no family scaling and no softcapping, and it does NOT delegate to `original(...)`. I forced that exact `else` block on CPU (monkeypatching `_fused_linear_ce_loss_is_supported` to False, which is one of the two ways the gate declines and lands in the same block) on models patched through the real `opaque.patches.apply_model_patches(compat=True, performance=True)`: llama native 4.862547 / fused 4.862547 / fallback 4.862547 (max|dlogit| 0.0); cohere native 4.850454 / fused 4.850454 / fallback 4.833583 (max|dlogit| 0.665); granite(logits_scaling=8.0) native 4.852680 / fused 4.852680 / fallback 4.862577 (max|dlogit| 0.344); gemma2 with final_logit_softcapping=30 shows no difference at random-init logit magnitudes. So the fused branch is exact and only the fallback drifts. Reachability verified: (a) the wrapper is installed for these families - Cohere, Cohere2, Granite and Gemma2 are all in `_FUSED_CE_CAUSAL_LM` (cross_entropy.py:122-140) so `_fused_linear_ce_supports_class` is True, and _factory.py:374-393 installs it whenever `fused_linear_cross_entropy` is not disabled, with `_dp_trainer.py:844-850` always calling `apply_model_patches(..., performance=True)`; (b) the loss-only marker is on at defaults - `_dp_trainer.py:868-874` sets `_fused_forward_uses_marker` unless `performance_kernels_config['fused_linear_cross_entropy'] is False`, and :2437-2442 adds `loss_only=True` to every non-logits DP loss call; (c) the guard at :199-217 (`if labels is None or not loss_only: return original(...)`) means the fallback is NOT hit by ordinary inference or logits-consuming calls - so, contrary to a first reading, this is not a universal fidelity break; (d) the remaining trigger is `hidden_states.is_cuda and dtype not in (bf16, fp16)`, i.e. CUDA with fp32 hidden states. `_setup_precision` (:877-905) defaults `_amp_dtype = None` (bf16=False) and never casts the model, so an fp32-loaded model on CUDA trivially produces fp32 hidden states and the fallback runs every step. I additionally measured that the last hidden state stays torch.float32 even under `torch.autocast(dtype=bfloat16)` for both Llama and Cohere (the fp32 embedding residual stream plus a norm that returns input_dtype), which would widen the trigger to bf16-autocast runs as well - that measurement was on CPU, so treat the autocast widening as likely-but-unexecuted; the plain fp32-on-CUDA trigger needs no such reasoning. Test gap confirmed: test_fused_ce_text_family_parity.py:18-54 fixtures are olmo2/olmo3/smollm3/ministral/glm4 (none scaled), and the scaling tests at :199-260 and :263-320 install a `loss_function` that raises `AssertionError('fallback should not run')`, i.e. they pin the fused branch only. Corrections to the report: the 'returned logits are unscaled' half is overstated - the fallback only executes on calls that set loss_only=True, and every in-repo caller of that marker sets it exactly when it is discarding logits (_dp_trainer.py:2437-2442, _sft_trainer.py:586-592), so no consumer reads those logits; the defect is the loss (and its gradient). My forced-branch numbers differ from the report's (native 4.850454 vs 4.853949 etc.) because of init/seed, not substance. Not tracked: open #880 (CUDA marker coverage for linear-CE kernel tests) is adjacent test-coverage work, and #862 (upcasting logits to fp32) is a numerics/perf request; neither covers family scaling in the declined branch. Severity high, not critical: no privacy guarantee is involved and it needs a logit-scaled family, but the trigger config (GPU, fp32 model, DPTrainer defaults) is ordinary and nothing warns.
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: DP fine-tuning a Cohere/Cohere2/Granite (logits_scaling != 1) checkpoint on CUDA with fp32 parameters - the DPTrainer default, since `bf16=False` leaves `_amp_dtype=None` and the model is never cast. `hidden_states.dtype` is then torch.float32 on a CUDA tensor, so `use_fused_ce` (cross_entropy.py:282-289) is False and every loss-only DP step falls into the `else` branch at :356-364, which projects `self.lm_head(hidden_states)` and calls `self.loss_function` with no `logit_scale` / `logits_scaling` / `final_logit_softcapping`. The per-example loss and its gradient are therefore computed from logits that are 16x too large for Cohere (logit_scale=0.0625) or 8x too small for Granite(8.0) - forced-branch measurement on this tree: cohere native 4.850454 vs fallback 4.833583 with max per-logit difference 0.665; granite(8.0) 4.852680 vs 4.862577, max difference 0.344; llama and un-softcapped families bit-identical. Nothing warns, and the fused branch that does apply the scaling is exact, so the divergence appears only on the declined path. Unverified link: I could not execute the CUDA+fp32 condition (no GPU in this sandbox) - I entered the identical `else` block via the other decline condition instead. No privacy impact; the loss returned to the optimizer is simply a different objective.

verdicts.title: Adaptive clipping releases a {0,1} clipped-count query while AdaClip accounting prices it at the {-1/2,+1/2} sensitivity, under-pricing the quantile release 2x in mu (4x in variance)
verdicts.reasoning: Both halves verified independently in the current tree. Runtime: `_clipped_fun.py:362-366` releases `num_clipped = float((norms > effective_cn).sum().item())` and `clipping_rate = num_clipped / float(batch_size)` (and :383-393 the same per group); `_adaptive.py:99-108` recomputes the same 0/1 count, and :111-122 `_sample_noisy_clipping_rate` returns `clipping_rate + randn()*fraction_noise_std`. The per-group loop at :546-575 and :580-607 does the same with a per-group folded key. `_distributed.py` likewise divides the global count by the realized global batch and adds the same noise. Grepping the whole repo, nothing anywhere subtracts 0.5 from the indicator, and no test pins the released statistic's sensitivity against the accountant. Accountant: `adaclip.rs:30-34` returns `(1/z^2 + k/(4*sigma_b^2)).sqrt()` and `_adaclip.py:78-80` sets `sigma_b = expected_batch_size * fraction_noise_std`, so the quantile term is `k*(0.5/sigma_b)^2` - a per-record count sensitivity of 1/2 (the non-Gaussian branch at :123-126 composes `_native.gaussian_pld(2.0*sigma_b, ...)`, which is the same assumption). That /4 is Andrew et al.'s `z = (z_Delta^-2 + (2 z_b)^-2)^-1/2`, valid only with the +/-1/2 shift TF Privacy's quantile_estimator_query implements (`below = cast(record <= estimate) - 0.5`, GaussianSumQuery with l2_norm_clip=0.5). Worked the adjacency out myself rather than trusting the citation: under Opaque's documented add-or-remove adjacency a {0,1} indicator sum moves by up to 1 when a record is added, so the released rate's sensitivity is <= 1/(n+1) ~ 1/W (max over clipped/unclipped of (n-c)/(n(n+1)) and c/(n(n+1))), giving mu_b = 1/(W*fraction_noise_std) = 1/sigma_b, exactly twice what the accountant charges; with the shift it would be 0.5/sigma_b and the formula would be right. Direction is anti-conservative (reported epsilon too small). Reproduced the magnitude with the repo's own accountant and prebuilt Rust extension by halving fraction_noise_std (equivalent to doubling mu_b), delta=1e-5, plain Poisson: (nm=1.1, W=256, N=50000, K=1, T=1000) reported 0.7316 vs corrected 0.7354 (+0.5%); (same, K=8) 0.7405 vs 0.7718 (+4.2%); (nm=0.8, W=64, N=50000, K=4, T=2000) 0.5791 vs 0.8467 (+46%); (nm=0.8, W=32, N=20000, K=8, T=1000) 1.3536 vs 5.3562 (3.96x); (nm=0.6, W=32, N=20000, K=16, T=1000) 4.6988 vs 16.1743 (3.44x) - the reporter's figures reproduce exactly. Reachability: `_dp_trainer.py:4471-4480` wires `dpsgd_acc.adaclip(gaussian(nm), expected_batch_size=..., num_groups=...)` whenever `clipping_mode == 'adaptive'`, and `_CLIPPING_KWARGS['adaptive'] = {'target_quantile','clipping_norm_max'}` (_training_arguments.py:213-217) so `fraction_noise_std` is the shared 0.05 default on both sides; the library recipe in docs/user-guide/clipping.md:230-249 and :481-495 (per-group) is the same pairing, and neither the docs nor the accountant docstring mentions any 1/2 shift. Refutation attempts that failed: no compensating factor elsewhere (the noise is applied to the rate, so absolute count noise is exactly batch_size*fraction_noise_std, matching the accountant's sigma_b definition); no test pins this; `test_adaptive.py:349-356` only checks the clipped-fraction convention, not sensitivity. Not tracked as open: the nearest issue, #345 'Bind AdaClip released statistic to the parameters the accountant charges', is in the 2026-08-27 open snapshot but is absent from the 2026-09-13 open lists and an earlier verification pass in this audit recorded it closed as not_planned, so it is not an open tracked item. Severity high rather than critical: `clipping_mode` defaults to 'fixed' (_training_arguments.py:560) so adaptive clipping is opt-in, and the epsilon error is only ~0.5% for a single group at a large batch; it reaches 3-4x only with many per-group quantile releases at small batches.
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: Any run that pairs `adaptive_clipped_grad` with `dpsgd_acc.adaclip(...)` - including DPTrainer with `clipping_mode='adaptive'`, which wires that pairing itself at the shared default fraction_noise_std=0.05. The runtime releases `num_clipped/batch_size + N(0, 0.05^2)` from a 0/1 clipping indicator (per-record sensitivity ~1/W), while the accountant prices the release at sensitivity 1/(2W) (`k/(4*sigma_b^2)` in adaclip.rs:33 with sigma_b = expected_batch_size*0.05). The quantile term's mu is therefore understated by exactly 2x (4x in variance) and the reported epsilon is not an upper bound. Measured with the repo's accountant at delta=1e-5: single-group default (nm=1.1, W=256, N=50000, T=1000) reports 0.7316 against a correctly-priced 0.7354 (0.5% low); per-group configurations - documented and supported at docs/user-guide/clipping.md:481-495 - are much worse because num_groups multiplies the mispriced term: K=8 at W=32, nm=0.8, T=1000 reports 1.3536 against 5.3562 (3.96x low), and K=16 at nm=0.6 reports 4.6988 against 16.1743 (3.44x low). A second, smaller error compounds it: the runtime divides by the realized batch size while the accountant divides by the constant expected_batch_size, so a below-average Poisson draw raises the true sensitivity further.

verdicts.title: Resuming a DDP run restores rank 0's sampler key on every rank, so all ranks draw the same local indices and Poisson/b-min-sep/BnB amplification loses its independent-inclusion hypothesis
verdicts.reasoning: Mechanical collapse reproduced and the accounting consequence established rigorously at the single-step level. Chain verified line by line on the current tree: fresh build folds the rank (`_dp_trainer.py:3944-3949`, reached only when `ctx.current_sampler is None` at :3938); the snapshot carries an absolute key (`_poisson.py:210-222` stores `key_seed`/`key_impl`) and is written inside `if _distributed.should_save(a, self._ddp):` (:5151) which returns `ddp.is_world_zero` by default (`_distributed.py:211-222`), with `self._save_dp_runtime(staging_dir, ctx)` at :5196 inside that block, while the per-rank RNG snapshot at :5205-5210 is deliberately written by every rank; restore runs unconditionally on every rank (:1862-1877 `ctx.current_sampler = from_state_dict(ctx.current_sampler, saved_sampler_state)`) and `_from_state_dict_poisson` rebuilds from `RngKey(seed=int(sd['key_seed']), ...)` (:255-265) with no rank re-fold. Same absolute-key restore in dpftrl/_poisson.py:304, _b_min_sep.py:259 and _balls_in_bins.py:260 (spot-checked). Reproduced: `PoissonSampler(range(1000), 0.05, key=fold_in(key(7), r))` gives different first batches for r=0/1 ([19,29,42,...] vs [39,55,60,...]); after `from_state_dict(template_r, state_dict(rank0_sampler))` both ranks hold `RngKey(seed=12201757873983228112, impl='opaque_threefry_like')` and emit the byte-identical batch [20,43,76,86,160,197,215,224] - the reporter's exact batch. The accounting claim is the substantive part, and it holds. Post-resume the mechanism is Poisson(q) over local *positions*, each position carrying the W co-indexed records (shards are equal length because the dataset is trimmed to a multiple of world_size, :3886-3908), while the accountant models i.i.d. Bernoulli(q) over the global dataset (`sample_rate = expected_batch_size / effective_dataset_size`, :1490-1503). For a target record x at position p the other W-1 co-indexed records are in the batch iff x is, so x's inclusion indicator is not independent of the rest of the batch and the Poisson mixture no longer decomposes as (1-q)P + q(P shifted). I computed the achievable neighbouring pair directly - all records zero except the W-1 co-indexed ones set to +C v, giving P = (1-q)N(0,z^2) + q N((W-1)C, z^2) vs Q = (1-q)N(0,z^2) + q N(W C, z^2) - and evaluated its hockey-stick by quadrature at nm=1.1, q=0.01, C=1, W=8: delta(eps=1.0) = 9.6e-4 against the repo accountant's own single-step subsampled-Gaussian delta(1.0) = 1.3e-10 (and 2.0e-3 vs 2.7e-8 at eps=0.5). That is a rigorous, seven-orders-of-magnitude violation of the accounted bound for one step, so the in-code assertion at :3874-3877 that 'the per-record marginal stays Bernoulli(q) either way, so the privacy accounting is unaffected' is the wrong conclusion - marginal preservation is not what the amplification proof consumes. The 1000-step figures also reproduce: reported `(poisson(gaussian(1.1), 0.01)*1000).epsilon_at(1e-5)` = 1.5154 vs 20.4283 for the indicator-revealed mixture over K~Bin(1000,0.01) of mu=sqrt(K)/1.1 Gaussians (13.5x). The horizon number is an idealization (it assumes the per-step indicator is decoded with zero error; at W=8 the cluster separation is (W-1)/nm = 6.4 sigma, so per-step decoding error is ~7e-4) - the rigorous part of my verification is the single-step hockey-stick comparison, and the 13.5x should be read as approximate. Refutation attempts that failed: no guard refuses a sampler snapshot under world_size > 1; no per-rank sampler snapshot exists (unlike the RNG snapshot); no test covers post-resume cross-rank divergence (grep over packages/opaque-transformers/tests found none); `save_on_each_node=True` would only move the writer to each node's local zero, not make it per-rank. Partial mitigation to note: the mechanical behavior IS documented in-code at _dp_trainer.py:3879-3886 as a 'Resume caveat (multi-GPU only) ... tracked for the multi-GPU work and validated there', so a reader is warned the correlation returns - but the same comment block tells them the accounting is unaffected, which is the defect this finding actually adds. Not tracked as an open issue: the open lists carry no DDP sampler-resume item (#55-58 are FSDP2, blocked). Severity high, not critical: it needs world_size > 1 AND a resume-from-checkpoint, and the epsilon blow-up needs an adversary holding the co-indexed records on the other shards - but that is the standard DP threat model, both conditions are an ordinary long-run workflow, and nothing warns at runtime.
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: Multi-GPU DP-SGD (or DP-FTRL) run that is checkpointed and resumed. Only rank 0 writes `dp_state.pt` (should_save -> is_world_zero), the sampler snapshot stores an absolute stream key, and every rank restores it, so from the resume point on all ranks emit the identical local index set - reproduced directly: two rank-folded PoissonSamplers diverge on a fresh start but after `from_state_dict` with rank 0's snapshot both hold RngKey(seed=12201757873983228112) and yield the same batch [20,43,76,86,160,197,215,224]. The global batch is then the union of the W co-indexed records at each sampled local position, so each record's inclusion indicator is perfectly correlated with its W-1 shard-mates. Per-record marginals are still q, but Poisson amplification needs independence, and the accounted subsampled-Gaussian bound is violated: for the achievable neighbouring pair (all records zero except x's W-1 co-indexed shard-mates at +C in one direction), at nm=1.1, q=0.01, W=8 the single-step hockey-stick delta at eps=1.0 is 9.6e-4 versus the repo accountant's 1.3e-10 for the same step. Over T=1000 steps the reported epsilon is 1.5154 while the idealized indicator-revealed mechanism (K~Bin(1000,0.01) unamplified Gaussians, mu=sqrt(K)/1.1) needs 20.43 at delta=1e-5; the horizon ratio is approximate, the single-step violation is exact. All five sampler serializers restore a saved absolute key, so every sampling mode is affected; for cyclic-Poisson/balls-in-bins the shared key also fixes a common partition/bin assignment. The in-code comment at _dp_trainer.py:3874-3886 acknowledges the correlation but states the accounting is unaffected, so a reader is actively misinformed about the risk.
